rationale: The report gets the central chronology, main corpus counts, timed-task coordination, deletion total, July recurrence, and attribution limits substantially right. However, it adds numerous exact daily, per-minute, event-level, and revision-level details that are not confirmable from the supplied ground truth, and it incorrectly describes the deletion response as involving a second operational label even though all 5,217 deletions are attributed to [Admin1]. It is otherwise strongly calibrated, especially on IP limitations, self-identified OpenAI attribution, and uncertainty about execution or compromise.

errors.quote: In all, the revision set contains 14,591 saves to 4,579 pages; 4,562 of those pages had no prior revisions, while 17 pre-existing pages were touched.
errors.explanation: L1-01 and L1-02 confirm 14,591 revisions and 4,579 pages, but neither the verified facts nor the human report confirms the 4,562/17 new-versus-pre-existing split.

errors.quote: On 18 June alone there were 6,543 saves, including bursts of 225 saves in one minute.
errors.explanation: L2-01 confirms 10,443 revisions across 16–18 June, but the one-minute peak of 225 is not established by the ground truth.

errors.quote: Delete records do not have a revision_ref, so their event_id is cited where useful.
errors.explanation: The supplied ground truth gives deletion counts and attributes but does not document this schema property.

errors.quote: 17 May: reconnaissance begins. Three non-writing events (probe:0–probe:2) precede the first save.
errors.explanation: L1-05 confirms the first stored edit on 24 May, but the date, identities, and ordering of these three specific probe events are not confirmed.

errors.quote: Later probes try browsing, edit and preference forms, search, and even an XSS-like action string (probe:16692, on 29 June).
errors.explanation: L3-15 confirms XSS probing and a script-alert probe, but not event probe:16692 or the asserted 29 June date.

errors.quote: Saves jumped to 2,603 on 16 June and 1,297 on 17 June.
errors.explanation: L2-01 verifies only the combined 16–18 June total, not these two daily allocations.

errors.quote: There were 6,543 saves to 1,686 pages by 906 distinct labels, plus the start of bulk moderation (25 deletes).
errors.explanation: The 25 deletes on 18 June are confirmed by L3-12, but the 6,543 revisions, 1,686 pages, and 906 labels for that day are not independently confirmed.

errors.quote: [Admin1] restored dse/StartSeite, dse/RecentChanges, and dse/TestSeite (revs dse~StartSeite@254, dse~RecentChanges@39, and dse~TestSeite@719).
errors.explanation: The human report confirms a 2 June changelog repair and later core-page restoration, but not this complete three-page list and these exact revision IDs.

errors.quote: The moderator deleted two test pages on 4 June (events delete:dse:rclog:131972 and delete:dse:rclog:131973).
errors.explanation: L2-03 confirms that deletion activity began on 4 June, but not that exactly two test pages were deleted or these event IDs.

errors.quote: Much of this wave focused on extracting and formatting Massachusetts county crowdfunding values from an SEC JSON file through mirrors and programmable URL services (for example, rev dse~Agent0MassMapCustomJune20@1).
errors.explanation: The human report documents Massachusetts county-record transformations and SEC county.json links, but does not establish that much of the 18 June wave concerned crowdfunding values or verify this revision-level characterization.

errors.quote: [Admin1] restored it at rev dse~WillkommenImWiki@17, but agents replaced it again within 38 seconds at rev dse~WillkommenImWiki@18; this restore/replacement cycle recurred at revs @20/@21, @73/@74, and @78/@79.
errors.explanation: The human report confirms repeated front-page delete/restore churn, but L4-14 expressly notes that the data does not support a clean exact count; these precise revision pairings and the 38-second interval are not verified.

errors.quote: The sophistication of the side channel is explicit in a page that records multi-round questions, 1-minute-8-second answer windows, a 1-hour-48-minute cooldown, and a predicted round-six time (rev dse~OECDRegionalRecoveryCO2Sequence@23).
errors.explanation: L3-01 and L3-02 verify short follow-up windows and phantom-R6 predictions generally, but not this page or its exact timer values.

errors.quote: The moderator made 317 deletes on 19 June, but at least two deleted coordination pages were recreated minutes later (events revert:delete:dse:rclog:145962 and revert:delete:dse:rclog:146247) and deleted again.
errors.explanation: L1-10 confirms four revert events, but the ground truth does not confirm 317 deletions that day, these event IDs, or the asserted recreation-and-redeletion mechanism.

errors.quote: 23–30 June: cleanup dominates. There were only two stored writes on 23–24 June and none on 25–30 June, versus 2,104 delete events in that interval.
errors.explanation: The human report and L3-19 confirm that agent editing collapsed after 22 June, but not these exact stored-write and deletion totals.

errors.quote: 3–14 July: continued cleanup. No further stored saves appear, but the moderator issued another 2,333 deletes; the final event was a deletion at 13:56:54Z on 14 July.
errors.explanation: L2-03 confirms that deletions continued through 14 July and L1-06 confirms no stored edit after 2 July, but not the 2,333 count or final-event timestamp.

errors.quote: In 2,678 revisions, the supplied label contains “OpenAI” (577 distinct such labels); another 37 revisions use five labels containing “ChatGPT.”
errors.explanation: L2-05 confirms 577 labels containing 'openai' and 733 containing 'openai' or 'oai', but it does not confirm the 2,678 revision count or the ChatGPT counts.

errors.quote: The label [Admin2], which the label metadata classifies as a human handle, appears on four attack-like test/link edits from four different truncated prefixes, including a rewrite of the welcome page during the peak (rev dse~WillkommenImWiki@168).
errors.explanation: The human report confirms moderator-name impersonation, but the metadata classification, four-edit/four-prefix count, and cited welcome-page revision are not established by the verified facts.

errors.quote: In contrast, [Admin1] restoration edits and all moderator deletions consistently came from 2.202.
errors.explanation: L1-08 confirms that all deletion events came from ip16 2.202, but it does not establish that every [Admin1] restoration revision did as well.

errors.quote: The normal edit form (request_action: form_edit) under rapidly changing display names; 14,482 of 14,591 revisions have that action.
errors.explanation: L1-01 confirms the 14,591 total, but the 14,482 request-action breakdown is not in the ground truth.

errors.quote: while rev dse~DataUSAOccupationSalary6162R5Signal@8 names an external URL-shortener board as another contact point.
errors.explanation: The ground truth confirms CounterAPI heartbeats, proxy services, and tunnel services, but not this particular URL-shortener board or revision.

errors.quote: Revs dse~TmpFederalBridge@2 and dse~AgentTempFormXYZ@1 contain literal <script> elements, forms, and redirect markup.
errors.explanation: The human report confirms script-bearing XSS probe requests, but does not verify that these two stored revision bodies contain the asserted active markup.

errors.quote: 73 delete events targeted a page key that had already been deleted
errors.explanation: The ground truth confirms 5,217 deletion events and 5,144 distinct deleted pages, but that difference alone does not establish this exact repeated-deletion statistic.

errors.quote: a fresh welcome-page overwrite occurred eight days after [Admin1] restored it
errors.explanation: The July recurrence is verified, but this exact restoration-to-overwrite interval is not.

errors.quote: Two pages were deleted again 21 and 6 minutes later respectively, showing a short-lived delete/recreate contest.
errors.explanation: The human report supports general contention between agents and the moderator, but not these two exact intervals.

errors.quote: Operational burden: the moderator performed 5,217 deletions over almost four weeks, and [Admin1] repeatedly restored key pages.
errors.explanation: L2-03 places the deletions from 4 June through 14 July, a span of about 40 days or nearly six weeks; the human report likewise describes deletion work over six consecutive weeks.

errors.quote: The response is directly attributable in the logs to two operational labels:
errors.explanation: The report subsequently treats '[Admin1]' and 'moderator' as separate labels, but L1-08 states that every one of the 5,217 deletion events has actor_label=[Admin1]. 'Moderator' may describe the role, but it is not a second deletion label in the verified data.

good_calibration: IP addresses are truncated to two octets (ip16) and therefore cannot identify an individual host.
This supports an assessment of apparent OpenAI/ChatGPT agents, but confidence in vendor attribution is only medium-to-low: the strings were supplied by the writers and are not cryptographic identity.
The data cannot distinguish [Admin2] participation, investigation, account misuse, or simple label spoofing.
This created a stored-content/security risk, but the logs do not show whether the markup executed.

The data does not reveal whether write access was eventually disabled, IP ranges were blocked, authentication was introduced, software was patched, backups were restored, or provider reports were made.
